caveats: No public offering at all as of 2026-09-29: fluidstack.io is now a mission/recruiting site (no product, pricing, sign-up or contact-sales link); /pricing and /gpu-cloud return 404 (Wayback: /pricing 404 since at least 2026-01-28). The platform (docs.fluidstack.io: managed Kubernetes/Slurm, alpha instances API) serves existing contracted customers via a Technical Account Manager. Last published list prices (Wayback 2025-10-17, historic, not current): H100 SXM $2.10, H200 SXM $2.30, A100 80GB $1.30 per GPU-hour; B200/GB200 'On Request'.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

Instances API (v1alpha1, regional https://<region>.atlas.fluidstack.io) supports preemptible and ephemeral instances, CPU instance types (CLI default 'cpu.2x') and GPU types like 'h100.8x', plus start/stop. Prices, billing increment and preemptible discount are not published; access is contract-only.

Contract terms (T&Cs): fees set per Order, 'payable in advance', 'non-cancellable, non-refundable' unless the Order says otherwise; per-minute/per-hour fees may require an advance deposit and access 'may cease' if funds run out (hard stop); subscriptions auto-renew; renewal price increases of at least 3%/year allowed with 30 days notice.

max_session_h.note: Instances/clusters run until explicitly stopped/deleted (contract-based reserved/preemptible capacity); no documented maximum session duration.

image_oci.quote: image string Default: "image://ubuntu22.04" Operating system image for the instance
image_oci.note: Instances (fluidctl/Infrastructure API) boot from an OS image URI scheme (e.g. image://ubuntu22.04), not a Docker/OCI container image; no image_oci support documented.

snapshot.quote: post /instances, get /instances, get /instances/{id}, delete /instances/{id}, post /instances/{id}/actions/start, post /instances/{id}/actions/stop
snapshot.note: Infrastructure API route list has no snapshot/checkpoint/image-export endpoint for instances; feature not offered as documented.

snapshot_auto.note: Only plain start/stop actions exist; no auto-save/restore-state mechanism is documented.

persistent_disk.quote: ephemeral boolean Default: false Whether the instance is ephemeral
persistent_disk.note: Instances default to ephemeral=false, implying non-ephemeral instances retain their disk/state across stop/start; not explicitly spelled out beyond the flag.

volume_attach.quote: post /instances, get /instances, get /instance-types, get /capacity, get /capabilities, post /projects, post /kubernetes/clusters, post /slurm/clusters/{id}/users
volume_attach.note: Full Infrastructure API route list has no /volumes or /disks endpoints; no attachable-volume feature documented.

volume_shared.note: No volumes API exists at all, so multi-attach/shared volumes are not offered.

public_ipv4.note: The /instances API example returns only a private (10.0.0.x) address for compute instances; public IPs only appear on Kubernetes/Slurm login/master nodes (publicIP field), not on generic instances.

inbound_https.note: not offered: no HTTPS ingress/URL routing feature documented for instances; only a private IP and SSH access are described.

ingress_rules.quote: Projects provide both logical and network isolation for cloud resources.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: project-level network isolation is documented, but no per-port/security-group ingress control API or UI is described for instances.

egress_allowlist.quote: post /instances, get /instances, get /instance-types, get /capacity, get /capabilities, post /projects
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: no egress/security-group/firewall endpoints in the Infrastructure API; only project-level network isolation is documented.

nested_virt.quote: Fluidstack managed Kubernetes is an ultra-reliable bare metal container orchestration platform powering frontier model training and inference.
nested_virt.note: derived: current product provisions genuine bare-metal nodes (isolation: bare-metal) with root/sudo access, not VMs nested inside another hypervisor, so /dev/kvm is expected to be usable inside the machine like on any bare-metal Linux host; not explicitly confirmed in docs.

static_egress_ip.note: Instances only expose a private (10.0.0.x) IP by default; no static/fixed outbound IP feature, egress-IP endpoint, or NAT gateway option is documented anywhere in the Infrastructure API, CLI reference, or Kubernetes/Slurm/Projects docs.

usage_api.quote: Infrastructure API and Management API provide endpoints for instances, projects, clusters, and user management; no billing or usage endpoints exist. Pricing is contract-based.
usage_api.note: granularity: none; cost: no; FluidStack billing is handled entirely off-API through contracts with a Technical Account Manager. Pricing, billing increments, and preemptible discounts are not published. No per-instance, per-tag, or account-level usage API is documented.
